rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [16, 256, 256] with dim=1: outer_size=16, reduce_size=256, inner_size=256. Kernel launch: dim3 blocks(16, ceil(256/256))=dim3(16,1). Since blocks.y=1, blockIdx.y is always 0. Since blocks.z is unspecified (defaults to 1), blockIdx.z is always 0. Both original (blockIdx.y*256+threadIdx.x) and mutant (blockIdx.z*256+threadIdx.x) compute inner_idx=0*256+threadIdx.x=threadIdx.x.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes blockIdx.y to blockIdx.z in the inner_idx calculation. For the fixed input shape [16, 256, 256] with the reduction dimension that passed 112 test rounds, inner_size equals 256. The grid is launched with blocks.y = ceil(256/256) = 1, meaning blockIdx.y is always 0 for all thread blocks. Since blockIdx.z is implicitly 1 (not specified in dim3 constructor), blockIdx.z is also always 0. Therefore both expressions evaluate to threadIdx.x, making the mutation semantically equivalent. The mutation would only be detectable if inner_size > 256, causing multiple y-blocks to be launched.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The mutation swaps blockIdx.y for blockIdx.z, but both are 0 because grid.y=1 (inner_size=256 fits in one block of 256 threads) and grid.z=1 (implicitly). Would require inner_size > 256 to expose the bug, which requires changing input shapes or reduction dimension.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing coverage, ensure kernel launch configurations are tested with grid dimensions > 1 in all axes (x, y, z) that are used in index calculations. The current test configuration masks the bug because inner_size happens to fit perfectly within one thread block.
